Hi Lena — thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps on the audit/logging items you asked about: 

Summary of what we covered
- Redwood can produce per-request audit entries that capture who invoked the API, which model variant was used, timestamps, request IDs, and action types (generate, embed, rerank).
- We support exports in CSV, JSONL, and Parquet; exports can be scoped by date range and by request-id list.
- Retention: configurable per-customer; default platform retention is 13 months, can be extended under contract.
- Data residency: logs are stored in the region where customer's account is provisioned (you requested US-East).

Requested evidence & what we're delivering next
- You asked for a sample export showing fields and schema. Attached is a redacted sample (audit_log_sample.csv) that mirrors the raw export format.
- SOC2 evidence & artifact list: attaching SOC2-evidence-list.xlsx that maps audit trails to control IDs.
- We will also provide per-request access logs and an appendix describing our masking/pseudonymization approach for PII in logs.

Open questions for you (so we can prepare the exact slices)
1) Do you need the full prompt text in the logs, or is a prompt-hash acceptable? (Many customers request hashes for privacy.)
2) For PII-sensitive tenants, do you want redaction applied prior to export, or will your side do post-processing?
3) Any specific fields missing from the sample that you need (IP, SSO user_id, org_role)?

Next steps
- If you confirm the answers above, we can produce a 30-day export sample and a short technical deep-dive with our infra team next week.
- If it helps, I can loop in Vivek (security) and Karthik (solutions engineering) to provide the artifact bundle and an S3 presigned link to the sample export.

Requirements from Acme Security
- We need an export that includes: request_id, timestamp (UTC), user_principal (SSO email), action_type, model_id, prompt_hash, response_hash, token_count_request, token_count_response, region, and storage_bucket/object_id.

- Retention: need proof that logs are retained for at least 12 months and that they can be exported in bulk for eDiscovery. The 13-month default you mentioned is fine — we need written confirmation.
- Export formats: prefer JSONL for automated ingestion, but CSV is fine for smaller ad-hoc exports. Parquet is a plus.

Evidence request (timeline)
- Can you provide the sample export and SOC2 artifact list by EOD Wednesday (18 Feb)?
- We will follow up with our auditor next week; please include a contact for your SOC2 point of contact and any auditor-facing evidence package.

Also: please confirm the controls you use to limit who can download raw exports and whether exports themselves include unredacted PII by default.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call if needed.

Jasmine / Karthik — sending the details we discussed. Draft language and artifacts below; feel free to send to Acme as-is.

Retention and residency
- Platform default retention for audit logs: 13 months (390 days). Confirmed — we will include written confirmation in the artifact bundle. Logs are stored in the customer-provisioned region (US-East for Acme).

Export formats & schema (we supply sample CSV & JSONL)
- Formats available: JSONL (newline-delimited JSON), CSV, Parquet. For automated ingestion we recommend JSONL; Parquet for large historic exports.
- Proposed export schema (field list): request_id, utc_timestamp, sso_user_email, user_role, action_type, model_id, prompt_hash, response_hash, token_count_request, token_count_response, response_status, region, storage_object_path, requester_ip (redacted by default), redaction_applied (true/false), internal_requester_id, request_duration_ms

PII handling and access controls
- By default, exports and stored logs have prompt text redacted; we provide prompt_hash and response_hash.
- For incident response, customers can request a full-content export under a documented process that includes a written justification and temporary access window; such exports are only delivered to named contacts via a controlled S3 presigned URL and require explicit customer approval.
- Access controls: RBAC (role-based), signed download URLs, multi-factor auth for portal, download audit trail recorded as separate immutable entries (who downloaded what/when).

Evidence & auditor contact
- Attached: audit_log_sample.csv (redacted sample), SOC2-evidence-list.xlsx (map to control IDs and artifact descriptions).
- SOC2 point of contact: security-audit@redwood.ai (David Kim, Director of Security Compliance). We will include an auditor-facing package that includes the control mapping and sample exports.

Technical options for the customer
- JSONL sample: good for automated processing (one JSON object per line). We can add an extra field that contains a base64-encoded encrypted blob if they want full content encrypted at rest for eDiscovery exports.
- Export delivery: S3 presigned link (recommended) or secure SCP transfer for on-prem.

Attachment stubs included:
- audit_log_sample.csv (CSV, 14 KB)
- SOC2-evidence-list.xlsx (XLSX, 32 KB)

Let me know if you want any additional control language; I can draft a two-paragraph confirmation of retention and a short export-process runbook for their legal/audit team.
